notes:
Quorum: token-weighted commit-reveal voting on Sepolia.

Token. src/Quorum.sol declares name "Quorum", symbol "QRM" and decimals 18 as constants, matching the token block above. Its constructor takes no arguments and mints totalSupply (1_000_000_000 ether = 10^27 minor units) to msg.sender, so the whole supply lands on the deploying factory and no constructor moves it afterwards. There is no mint, burn, owner, admin, pause or upgrade path: the only balance-changing functions are transfer and transferFrom, approve touches allowances alone, and totalSupply is a compile-time constant, so it is fixed for the life of the contract.

Application contract. src/CommitRevealVote.sol is the single application contract and has no project-internal dependencies. Its constructor is `constructor(address token_)`, one nonpayable address parameter, filled by $token so the contract is bound to the launch token deployed in this same launch. The constructor reverts with InvalidToken() on the zero address and assigns the immutable `token`; it makes no external calls and reads no msg.sender, so nothing about the deploying factory is captured as a privileged identity.

Why there is no $owner reference. CommitRevealVote has no owner, admin, fee recipient, treasury or other privileged role, and therefore no constructor parameter a project owner could occupy. Ownership comes from policy alone; this manifest names no wallet and hard-codes no address. The absence of an $owner argument reflects the accepted source, not an omission.

No initialization calls are required. Every parameter the contract needs is set in the constructor: the token address is the contract's only configuration, and proposal timing is supplied per proposal by the caller of openProposal(bytes32 titleHash, uint64 commitDeadline, uint64 revealDeadline) rather than being configured at deployment. The timing bounds it enforces, MIN_PHASE_DURATION (1 hours) and MAX_PROPOSAL_DURATION (90 days), are compile-time constants, not deployment parameters, so no constructor argument or post-deployment call sets them. Anyone may open a proposal; there is no allowlist to seed.

Dependency order. Only one project contract exists, so the ordering requirement is trivially satisfied and no $contract: reference appears.

Constructor argument audit. Exactly one argument is declared above and exactly one is declared in the source. It is address-typed, the only argument type into which a reference may be placed, and $token is a backward reference to the launch token, deployed before the application contracts. No static words and no bytes32, uint or bool arguments appear in this manifest.

Pool. Paired against native ETH on Sepolia, expressed as the zero address, with fee 3000, tickSpacing 60 and initialPrice "79228162514264337593543950336", the sqrtPriceX96 for a 1:1 ratio. The pool has no hook. These are the policy's standard pool parameters and are not a statement about what QRM is worth.

Runtime and opcode profile. CommitRevealVote uses no proxy, no DELEGATECALL, no CALLCODE and no SELFDESTRUCT; its only external interaction is transfer/transferFrom on the immutable token address, guarded by a nonReentrant mutex and ordered checks-effects-interactions, with explicit return-value checks so a token returning false is treated as a failure. It declares no receive or fallback function, so it cannot hold ETH, and the only balances it manages are the QRM that voters lock while a ballot is outstanding; QRM transferred to it directly is not attributed to any ballot.

Scope. This manifest describes the accepted tree at src/Quorum.sol and src/CommitRevealVote.sol with ABI exports under docs/abi/. It carries no supply, allocation, owner, chain, policy-version or artifact-hash fields; those belong to policy, attestation and the deployer, which bind the published commit and creation bytecode after this stage. These notes are explanatory and confer no deployment authority.
